target_description: Predicted change to the next REAL calibration campaign. target_next_valeur_reference is always the next REAL chronological observation.
prediction_unit: UNKNOWN / requires confirmation - not recorded in source ILA data.
training_dataset: data/processed/ILA_train_augmente_features.csv (train real + safe augmented copies; TEST instruments never included)

held_out_test_evaluation.note: This number (instrument-disjoint GroupShuffleSplit, single seed=42) is kept as a secondary/reference metric. It is NOT the deployment decision criterion - see 'primary_validation_chronological' for the metric that determines beats_baseline.

evaluation_metrics_groupkfold.note: beats_baseline is now driven by PRIMARY CHRONOLOGICAL validation (see 'primary_validation_chronological' above), per project decision 2026-09-18: chronological future-of-known-instrument prediction is the real deployment scenario, not instrument-disjoint generalization. Under that validation, HuberRegressor (and all 13 other tested algorithms) fail to beat the persistence baseline, so beats_baseline=False and the API/UI now recommend the persistence baseline. The GroupShuffleSplit/robustness numbers below are KEPT for reference (secondary/robustness protocols, per project methodology) but are no longer the selection criterion.

known_limitations: PRIMARY CHRONOLOGICAL VALIDATION (2026-09-18): 0/14 algorithms beat the persistence baseline when evaluated on genuinely future, held-out-in-time observations of KNOWN instruments (MAE 0.626 for the best algorithm, Huber, vs 0.592 for simple persistence). Consequently NO ML model is currently recommended for production; the persistence baseline is the recommended prediction (recommended_source=baseline_persistence). See 'primary_validation_chronological' and experiments/audit_v3/model_comparison_PRIMARY_CHRONOLOGICAL.csv.

HuberRegressor was previously selected by an instrument-disjoint GroupShuffleSplit (single random 80/20 instrument split, seed=42, MAE=0.894) and confirmed only mildly robust under repeated splits (7/10 seeds, mean MAE 2.43 vs baseline 2.46 - see reports/quality/final_validation_audit.json). That protocol answers a different question (generalization to brand-new instruments) than this project's real use case (predicting a KNOWN instrument's future drift) and is retained here only as a secondary/robustness metric.

primary_validation_chronological.description: PRIMARY validation per project decision (2026-09-18): leakage-safe, per-instrument chronological split within the 17 TRAIN-pool instruments (older ~80% of each instrument's real observations = history/train, newest ~20% = held-out future/test). Synthetic augmented rows are fit ONLY on the history portion and never enter the historical sequence or the held-out future rows, which are 100% real.
primary_validation_chronological.method: per-instrument chronological split on chrono_rank_in_instrument, ~80% history / ~20% future
